evals.prompt: Write a Paramita (Python) program that places 8 queens on a chessboard so that none attack each other, and print one placement.
evals.expected_output: One-hot Boolean per cell with exactly-one rows and columns and at-most-one diagonals, solved with Cadical300, printing one board
assertions: Uses paramita.modelling Bool and add_to_container with to_cnf
Rows and columns are exactly-one (sum == 1) and diagonals at most one
Solves with SatSolver Cadical300 and prints a placement from model()

evals.prompt: Using Paramita in Python, list every way to put 6 non-attacking queens on a 6 x 6 board and print how many there are.
evals.expected_output: Enumeration with blocking clauses over the cell Booleans, printing the count 4
assertions: Enumerates with repeated solve() and a blocking clause
The blocking clause covers only the answer cell Booleans, not auxiliary variables
Stops when solve() returns False

evals.prompt: Solve a 0/1 knapsack with Paramita in Python: items (weight, value) (3, 30), (4, 50), (2, 40), capacity 7. Maximise the value and print the optimum.
assertions: Passes the objective to add_to_weighted_container, which maximises it
Reads the optimum as constant + benefit() and checks status OPTIMAL
Uses a PB constraint for the capacity

evals.prompt: Using Paramita in Python, find every selection of items that reaches the maximum value of a knapsack with weights 2, 2, 2, 4, values 3, 3, 3, 6, capacity 4.
evals.expected_output: Optimum 6 and four distinct optimal selections
assertions: Solves the optimum first with MaxSAT and checks the status is OPTIMAL
Posts objective == optimum to a fresh solver before enumerating
Enumerates over the item Booleans so each selection is printed once

evals.prompt: Colour a graph with Paramita in Python using as few colours as possible; read the graph from a JSON file given as the first argument.
evals.expected_output: Minimum colour count from a MaxSAT model over the negated number of used colours, reading the JSON file
assertions: Reads the file path from sys.argv and parses it with json
Minimises by passing the negated objective to add_to_weighted_container
Negates the result of constant + benefit()

evals.prompt: Show with Paramita in Python that 3 pigeons cannot each have their own hole when there are only 2 holes.
evals.expected_output: Program prints unsatisfiable from solve() returning False
assertions: Reads infeasibility from solve() returning False, not an exception
Uses at-most-one per hole and exactly-one per pigeon

evals.prompt: Schedule three jobs on one machine with Paramita in Python so that no two jobs overlap and each job meets its deadline; print the start times.
evals.expected_output: One-hot start times with a no-overlap constraint per time slot, printing a feasible schedule
assertions: Start times are one-hot per job with exactly-one
No overlap is at most one running job per time slot
Reads start times back from the model
